findings.claim: In May 2004 Gates agreed to pay an $800,000 civil penalty, in a complaint the FTC had the Justice Department file, for buying ICOS shares in 2002 without the premerger filing the Hart-Scott-Rodino Act requires. The FTC had sought no penalty for an earlier 2001 filing lapse over Republic Services shares; the matter is more than 20 years old.

In June 2001 the full D.C. Circuit upheld a finding that Microsoft illegally maintained its monopoly in PC operating systems, reversed the attempted-monopolisation finding, sent the tying claim back and vacated the remedy. The opinion describes conduct by Gates himself in dealings with Apple and Intel; the ruling is 25 years old.

The European Commission fined Microsoft €497 million in 2004 for withholding data from rivals and tying Media Player to Windows, then €280.5 million (2006) and €899 million (2008) for not complying; an EU court cut the 2008 fine to €860 million in 2012. In 2013 it fined Microsoft €561 million for breaking a browser-choice commitment, which Microsoft blamed on a technical error.

The New York Times reported in October 2024, citing people briefed, that Gates privately said he had given about $50 million to Future Forward USA Action, a group backing Kamala Harris that does not disclose its donors. Gates did not publicly confirm the gift.

A 2025 BMJ Global Health study found the Gates Foundation gave WHO $5.5 billion in 640 grants from 2000 to 2024, 9.5% of WHO revenue in 2010-2023, second only to the US, with almost 60% for polio. The authors say earmarked donor funds let donor-favoured areas draw more resources than others.

Justice Department releases include emails, calendar entries and photos documenting meetings with Epstein, which Gates says ran from 2011, after Epstein’s 2008 plea, to December 2014. Gates reportedly apologised to foundation staff in February 2026 and told a House committee on 10 June 2026 it was a grave error; he denies knowing of Epstein’s crimes and is not accused of any.

The files hold two unsent drafts dated 18 July 2013, from Epstein’s account, making sexual allegations about Gates; his spokesperson calls them absurd and false, and Gates told lawmakers they suggest Epstein contemplated blackmail. Lawmakers said in 2026 that about 3.5 million of more than 6 million identified pages had been released.

A WilmerHale review for the foundation, released in July 2026 as a three-page summary, found Gates and staff met Epstein about 30 times in 2011-2014 despite staff concerns, and found no payments to him and no evidence of knowledge of his crimes. It did not cover Gates’s personal communications or personal-capacity dealings with Epstein.

The Gates Foundation says it distributed more than $100 billion in its first 25 years, to 2025, for vaccines, infectious disease, nutrition and education, and plans to spend about $200 billion more before closing in 2045. Warren Buffett has given it more than $47 billion in Berkshire stock since 2006.

politics.reason: The Gates Foundation gave WHO $5.5 billion from 2000 to 2024 and was its second-largest funder in 2010–2023; a 2025 study found these earmarked grants, almost 60% for polio, shape which programmes get funded. The New York Times reported in 2024 that Gates privately said he gave about $50 million to a group backing Kamala Harris that does not disclose its donors; he did not confirm it publicly.

social.reason: In 2001 a US appeals court upheld a finding that Microsoft illegally maintained its monopoly in PC operating systems; the opinion describes Gates’s own conduct in dealings with Apple and Intel. EU regulators fined Microsoft repeatedly from 2004 to 2013 over interoperability, bundling and browser choice. These are company acts more than ten years old; this research did not check Microsoft’s current conduct.

legal.reason: Paid a personal $800,000 civil penalty in 2004 to settle FTC charges that he bought ICOS shares in 2002 without a required premerger filing. At company level, a US appeals court upheld in 2001 that Microsoft illegally maintained a monopoly, and the European Commission fined Microsoft €497 million (2004), €280.5 million (2006), €899 million (2008, cut to €860 million) and €561 million (2013). All are over ten years old.

unresolved.reason: Released Epstein files document meetings and correspondence after Epstein’s conviction; Gates calls them a grave error, apologised to foundation staff and told a House committee in 2026 he never saw signs of ongoing crimes. Unsent 2013 drafts by Epstein make sexual allegations his spokesperson calls false; no authority has substantiated them. A 2026 foundation review found about 30 meetings and no payments, but did not cover his personal communications. Lawmakers say many pages remain unreleased.

proposal.counterweights: The Gates Foundation says it distributed more than $100 billion in its first 25 years, to 2025, including $5.5 billion to WHO; Warren Buffett has given it more than $47 billion in Berkshire stock since 2006.
proposal.rationale: Legal 0→3: a personal $800,000 FTC civil penalty in 2004 (R2, Dell precedent), though over 20 years old. Social 1→3: the rubric names a court-established monopoly, and the 2001 ruling upheld one for Microsoft and describes Gates’s own conduct; 2 is arguable given its age. Politics stays 2. Unresolved stays 3: no pending case names him (R6), but released documents leave questions; the foundation review is complete. Reuters (Feb 2026) and the Boston 25 AP copy could not be opened; CBS and WTOP replace them.
